product_findings.action: Define the exact command(s), required/optional flags, exit code behavior, and deterministic summary fields (applied/merged/skipped/conflicts, rerun status, log path).
product_findings.risk: The spec uses placeholders like "relevant CLI command/step," so users cannot reliably know what to run, what output means success, or what constitutes a safe rerun.
product_findings.title: CLI contract is not explicit enough for users to execute confidently

product_findings.action: Add automated tests for first-run and rerun behavior across clean and conflicted repos; assert deterministic no-op/expected changes and user-facing rerun summary output.
product_findings.risk: Without explicit automated idempotency checks, users can see inconsistent outcomes on second run and lose trust in bootstrap safety.
product_findings.title: Core promise of safe re-runs is not acceptance-tested

product_findings.action: Specify deterministic prompt copy with safe default, preview impacted files before apply, explicit confirmation for destructive paths, and cancel/retry guidance aligned with SEC-01 protected-path constraints.
product_findings.risk: Overwrite/merge/skip is named but decision safety is unclear, increasing accidental destructive outcomes under time pressure.
product_findings.title: Conflict handling UX is under-specified for destructive choices

product_findings.action: Require fail-closed preflight checks before writes and standardize blocking error messages to include remediation and explicit rerun-safety status.
product_findings.risk: For missing dependencies or non-git targets, users may not know if partial state exists or whether rerun is safe, causing workflow stalls.
product_findings.title: Recovery contract for failure states is incomplete

product_findings.action: Replace placeholders with measurable targets and map each acceptance criterion to concrete automated-test or human-validation evidence.
product_findings.risk: The `{feature['outcome']}` placeholder and "user confirmation" measurement make completion criteria ambiguous and prone to premature sign-off.
product_findings.title: Acceptance quality is weakened by unresolved template and subjective metrics

product_findings.action: Run human validation on at least: clean repo bootstrap, conflicted repo choice flow, and non-git path failure; require explicit PO sign-off.
product_findings.risk: Automated checks alone will not confirm that a Developer/PO can interpret prompts and next steps correctly in realistic repos.
product_findings.title: No explicit human validation gate for end-user clarity

security_findings.action: Resolve target/destination with canonical paths, reject any write that escapes repo root after resolution, and block writes through symlinked paths with a fail-closed error.
security_findings.risk: The feature requires copying into a target repo, but the spec does not define canonical path or symlink checks. A crafted path/symlink can cause writes outside the repo root.
security_findings.title: Missing repo-boundary and symlink escape controls

security_findings.action: Implement protected path rules: hard-deny `.git/**`, default-skip sensitive patterns, and require explicit opt-in with deterministic confirmation for any protected overwrite.
security_findings.risk: Conflict handling is defined as overwrite/merge/skip, but no restricted path set is defined. Security-critical files (e.g., `.git/**`, secret env files, hooks, CI security config) could be overwritten.
security_findings.title: No protected-path policy for overwrite/merge/skip

security_findings.action: Enforce offline behavior by default (no network subprocesses), require explicit flag for any remote source, and log source provenance in run output.
security_findings.risk: The spec states local-only/no remote transfer, but no technical control is defined to prevent network egress during bootstrap.
security_findings.title: Local-only security requirement is not enforced

security_findings.action: Normalize file modes on write, allow executable bit only for approved script paths, and strip suid/sgid bits.
security_findings.risk: Copy/merge behavior does not define safe permission handling; unsafe executable bits or special mode bits could be propagated into the target repo.
security_findings.title: Permission and executable-bit hardening is unspecified

security_findings.action: Add negative automated tests for all mandatory controls and make them required in the feature test gate.
security_findings.risk: Current tests are generic and do not validate traversal/symlink escapes, protected-path overwrite blocking, offline enforcement, or permission hardening, leaving controls vulnerable to regression.
security_findings.title: Security regression coverage is absent in test scenarios

product_findings.action: Define explicit, testable output/state requirements for each gate (Plan, Patch, Test, Report), including required status labels, offload/log pointers, and remediation messaging.
product_findings.risk: Core requirements and tests are too generic ('perform workflow action'), so different implementations can pass while producing inconsistent CLI behavior, reducing user trust and making failures hard to recover.
product_findings.title: Gate behavior is not specified as a deterministic user contract

product_findings.action: Reconcile specs to one canonical HIGH-risk approval interaction aligned with SEC-02-001, then update tests and user-facing copy accordingly.
product_findings.risk: UX constraints require a simple 'y/n' approval prompt while security requires typed ticket confirmation with identity/timestamp (SEC-02-001). This conflict will create rework and unclear user expectations at the most critical gate.
product_findings.title: Approval UX conflicts with security-required HIGH-risk approval flow

product_findings.action: Add automated tests for fail-safe rerun behavior, including state integrity after failed tests and required summary markers (resumed/skipped/repaired/newly executed).
product_findings.risk: Feature says failures should allow a clean retry, but no automated assertions define what must be preserved, reset, or re-run. Users can face partial-state confusion and inconsistent rerun outcomes.
product_findings.title: Retry/resume acceptance quality is underspecified

product_findings.action: Require PO human validation of blocking UX copy across happy/unhappy paths (HIGH-risk approval, missing preconditions, test failure, retry guidance) before completion.
product_findings.risk: Technical implementation may pass while the Developer/PO still finds blocking prompts and recovery instructions ambiguous, leading to workflow stalls or incorrect actions.
product_findings.title: No explicit end-user sign-off gate for blocking prompt clarity

product_findings.action: Replace placeholder metrics with concrete targets and measurement method tied to logs/offload artifacts.
product_findings.risk: A placeholder metric remains (`{feature['outcome']}`), so user value cannot be objectively verified and acceptance may become subjective.
product_findings.title: Success metrics are not measurable

security_findings.action: Require interactive TTY approval with an explicit typed confirmation containing the ticket ID, record approver OS user + timestamp in run metadata, and fail closed in non-interactive contexts. Add tests for missing/invalid approval paths.
security_findings.risk: The UX requires a simple `y/n` approval prompt for HIGH-risk work, but no control ties approval to a human PO identity; an automated actor could self-approve and bypass the intended gate.
security_findings.title: HIGH-risk approval gate is not identity-bound

security_findings.action: Implement pre-write redaction for common secret patterns and configured project patterns, suppress raw secret-bearing env output, and add regression tests asserting masking behavior.
security_findings.risk: Workflow output is written to `.offload/<id>.txt` and `logs/<WI>/<step>.log` with no stated scrubbing, so credentials/tokens printed by tools or tests can be persisted and exposed.
security_findings.title: Offload/log artifacts lack secret redaction controls

security_findings.action: Enforce strict allowlist regex for IDs/step names, canonicalize and verify resolved paths remain under approved directories, and reject `..`, absolute paths, and separator variants. Add negative-path tests.
security_findings.risk: The design uses dynamic path parts like `<WI>` and `<step>` but defines no validation/canonicalization, enabling path traversal or overwrite outside approved logging roots.
security_findings.title: Dynamic log path inputs are not constrained against traversal

security_findings.action: Define per-stage command allowlists and argument schemas, execute via structured argv (no shell interpolation), and fail closed on unknown commands. Add tests proving denied commands are blocked.
security_findings.risk: Requirements say to run the relevant CLI/tooling step but do not define allowed commands/args, creating risk of unintended or injected command execution during role handoffs.
security_findings.title: Workflow execution lacks explicit command allowlisting

security_findings.action: Create artifact directories/files with restrictive permissions (`0700`/`0600`) and add automated checks to enforce expected modes on macOS.
security_findings.risk: Local-only operation does not prevent data exposure if `.offload`/`logs` files are created with permissive defaults on shared hosts.
security_findings.title: Permissions for local security-relevant artifacts are unspecified

product_findings.action: Define and document deterministic mode semantics with concrete CLI examples: default conservative behavior, `--reapply` overwrite scope, protected-path precedence, and exit code meanings.
product_findings.risk: The spec does not clearly define the exact CLI contract for default mode vs `--reapply` (what is overwritten, what is always skipped, and expected exit outcomes), creating a high risk of unintended destructive use.
product_findings.title: Reapply mode contract is ambiguous for end users

product_findings.action: Expand automated tests to assert before/after file states, per-file applied/skipped reporting, idempotent reruns, and alignment with required security guardrail scenarios in `SEC-03-004`.
product_findings.risk: Current test scope is primary-path only; it does not prove user-facing guarantees for overwrite summaries, rerun safety, and deterministic outcomes, so regressions can ship unnoticed.
product_findings.title: User-visible acceptance quality is not testable yet

product_findings.action: Require deterministic failure output that includes: what was applied, what was skipped, why execution stopped, exact safe rerun command, and whether cleanup is required.
product_findings.risk: Users are told retry is safe, but required failure output is not explicit; without clear remediation and rerun guidance, recovery becomes manual and error-prone.
product_findings.title: Partial-failure recovery UX is underspecified

product_findings.action: Specify gate behavior by mode: interactive/default path vs non-interactive `--reapply`, with mandatory conflict/overwrite summaries in output when prompts are suppressed.
product_findings.risk: The UX blueprint references review/conflict gates while `--reapply` is non-interactive; without explicit per-mode gate behavior, implementation will drift and confuse users.
product_findings.title: Workflow gate behavior conflicts are unresolved

product_findings.action: PO/end-user must review and approve the protected-path inventory and exceptions, then record the decision in `docs/03-logs` before final sign-off.
product_findings.risk: Even with defaults, repository-specific critical files may be missed, leaving residual overwrite risk in local environments.
product_findings.title: Repo-specific protected-path sign-off is missing

security_findings.action: In patching, resolve each target with canonical path checks, reject path traversal, and fail closed on symlinked targets (or enforce a strict symlink policy) before any write.
security_findings.risk: The spec requires deterministic overwrite in `--reapply` mode but does not require canonical path checks. A crafted path (`../`) or symlinked target could cause writes outside the repository and overwrite arbitrary local files.
security_findings.title: Reapply write path is not constrained to repo root

security_findings.action: Implement an explicit protected-path policy (denylist/allowlist with precedence) and enforce it before overwrite decisions; include deterministic skip reporting for every protected file.
security_findings.risk: Requirement 1 says to preserve protected paths, but no concrete protected-path rules are defined while Requirement 2 enables promptless overwrite. Sensitive files can be overwritten if not explicitly guarded.
security_findings.title: Protected-path policy is underspecified for non-interactive overwrite

security_findings.action: Use temp-file writes plus atomic rename, record resumable state, and ensure retries are idempotent and fail closed when state is inconsistent.
security_findings.risk: Edge Case 2 requires safe retry, but no atomic write/checkpoint mechanism is defined. Interrupted reapply can leave mixed template states that execute inconsistent or unsafe scripts.
security_findings.title: Partial failure safety lacks atomic reapply controls

security_findings.action: Add automated tests that must pass for: path traversal rejection, symlink boundary enforcement, protected-path non-overwrite, and safe retry after forced interruption.
security_findings.risk: `TASK-401` only requires primary-path coverage; there are no required tests for traversal, symlink abuse, protected-path enforcement, or partial-failure recovery under `--reapply`.
security_findings.title: Security guardrail tests are missing from task plan

security_findings.action: During human validation, review and approve the protected-path inventory for this repo and log the decision in `docs/03-logs`.
security_findings.risk: Default protected paths may miss repository-specific credential files, causing accidental overwrite in local environments.
security_findings.title: Repo-specific secret path review is not explicitly required

product_findings.action: Update spec and implementation to fail-closed by default when pointer generation fails, show concise remediation guidance, and allow stdout fallback only via explicit opt-in.
product_findings.risk: Current behavior allows pointer-missing cases to continue with stdout fallback, which defeats the feature promise (token efficiency and consistent gated workflow) and can expose noisy/sensitive output inline.
product_findings.title: Fail-open pointer handling breaks user trust in offload enforcement

product_findings.action: Define and enforce explicit offload eligibility rules (e.g., size/line thresholds and command classes), document them in feature docs, and surface them in CLI preflight/status text.
product_findings.risk: Users cannot predict when offload will trigger, so behavior may vary by command/run and reduce confidence in workflow gates.
product_findings.title: No deterministic definition of "noisy output" creates inconsistent UX

product_findings.action: Standardize blocking error messages to include immediate remediation and rerun-safety status; add tests that assert this copy is emitted for failure scenarios.
product_findings.risk: On write failure or missing `.offload/`, users may not know exact next steps or whether rerun is safe, increasing retry errors and abandoned runs.
product_findings.title: Recovery-path UX is underspecified and may stall users

product_findings.action: Expand TASK-401 coverage to include pointer-missing failure mode, missing offload directory recovery, below-threshold behavior, and explicit no-large-output-to-stdout assertions.
product_findings.risk: Primary-path-only coverage can miss regressions where large output leaks inline, pointer IDs are absent, or edge behavior diverges from UX constraints.
product_findings.title: Test plan does not guarantee end-user outcomes

product_findings.action: Replace placeholder success metric with concrete measurable targets and pass/fail thresholds tied to logs and automated checks.
product_findings.risk: Placeholder metrics and generic DoD criteria allow subjective completion without proving reduced workflow errors or token waste.
product_findings.title: Acceptance quality is not measurable

product_findings.action: Run human validation on one happy path and two failure paths to confirm pointer discoverability, clarity of next actions, and acceptable debug speed; record explicit PO sign-off.
product_findings.risk: Even if technically correct, users may find pointer lookup and next-step handoff unclear and bypass the intended workflow.
product_findings.title: Human usability sign-off is required for pointer-first debugging flow

security_findings.action: Change pointer-missing handling to fail-closed for offload-eligible commands (non-zero exit), emit only minimal remediation metadata, and require explicit opt-in for any stdout fallback.
security_findings.risk: The feature spec error table states "Pointer id missing -> Fallback to stdout -> Continue". If offload fails, full noisy output can be emitted inline to prompts/logs, which can leak secrets and bypass the offload gate.
security_findings.title: Fail-open pointer-missing path exposes raw command output

security_findings.action: Enforce secure permissions (`0700` dirs, `0600` files), verify `.offload/` and sensitive logs are ignored by git templates, and add deterministic cleanup/retention handling.
security_findings.risk: The docs require writing `.offload/<id>.txt` and `logs/<WI>/<step>.log` but define no file permission, ignore-list, or retention controls. Sensitive command output may be readable by other local users or accidentally committed.
security_findings.title: Offload artifacts lack confidentiality controls

security_findings.action: Generate IDs internally, validate against a strict allowlist, canonicalize target paths under `.offload`, reject symlinks/non-regular files, and use exclusive file creation.
security_findings.risk: Requirement 2 defines pointer IDs but does not require strict ID validation or canonical path checks. Crafted IDs or symlinked offload directories can cause path traversal or writes outside the intended location.
security_findings.title: Pointer ID and path safety requirements are missing

security_findings.action: Add automated tests for pointer-missing failure mode, missing-offload-dir recovery, path traversal/symlink attempts, and no-large-output-to-stdout guarantees; gate completion on these tests.
security_findings.risk: TASK-401 only targets primary-path coverage; it does not require tests for fail-closed behavior, permission enforcement, traversal/symlink rejection, or output-leak prevention.
security_findings.title: Security regression tests are not required by current task plan

product_findings.action: Define and implement a strict CLI message contract for each Plan/Patch/Test/Report transition and failure state, including role, stage, artifact pointer, and explicit remediation; add output assertions.
product_findings.risk: The feature does not define deterministic CLI outputs per gate/role, so users may not know current stage, required artifact, or exact next action, increasing skipped-gate and recovery errors.
product_findings.title: Gate UX contract is underspecified for end users

product_findings.action: Add automated tests for conflicting-role outputs, skipped-gate fail-safe behavior, loopback-to-planner routing, and interrupted-run resume semantics with pass/fail expectations.
product_findings.risk: Current scenarios miss conflict resolution, gate-skip prevention, reviewer/tester failure loopbacks, and resume behavior, so regressions can ship while the workflow appears nominal.
product_findings.title: Acceptance tests do not cover critical workflow failure loops

product_findings.action: Require human validation artifacts for PO decisions (run_id, decision, rationale, timestamp) and make completion contingent on that record.
product_findings.risk: Conflict adjudication and HIGH-risk approvals can be treated as implicit decisions, weakening PO control and creating user-trust and accountability gaps.
product_findings.title: Human decision points are not explicitly captured as sign-off artifacts

product_findings.action: Update blocked/error UX to include missing prerequisite slugs, next valid command/action, and rerun-safety guidance; verify in tests.
product_findings.risk: Messages like 're-run required step' without prerequisite identifiers or next eligible action create repeated failed attempts and avoidable user friction.
product_findings.title: Blocked-state recovery guidance is too vague

product_findings.action: Replace placeholder metrics with measurable thresholds and evidence sources in feature docs and validation logs.
product_findings.risk: A placeholder metric and non-quantified targets prevent objective validation that user pain (workflow failures/confusion) was reduced.
product_findings.title: Success metrics are not measurable

security_findings.action: Add a per-run artifact manifest (run_id, role, timestamp, SHA-256 for each artifact) and verify it at every gate transition; fail closed on any mismatch.
security_findings.risk: The spec requires Plan/Patch/Test/Report artifacts to be archived before gate transitions, but it does not require checksums/signatures. A compromised or buggy sub-agent could alter evidence after generation and the orchestrator could advance on forged results.
security_findings.title: Gate artifacts are not integrity-protected

security_findings.action: Enforce role-based path allowlists/denylists in the orchestrator runner and reject out-of-scope writes with explicit errors.
security_findings.risk: Docs describe role separation and role-scoped outputs, but no technical control is specified to prevent cross-role file writes (for example, patcher modifying reviewer/tester artifacts). This enables privilege escalation inside the workflow.
security_findings.title: Role boundaries are defined but not enforceably sandboxed

security_findings.action: Require interactive TTY for HIGH-risk approval, bind approval to current run_id, and persist an approval audit record before unblocking.
security_findings.risk: The UX requires an explicit `y/n` approval and `Awaiting PO Approval`, but no control is defined to ensure approval is interactive and tied to the current run. Piped input or automation could unintentionally approve blocked work.
security_findings.title: HIGH-risk approval gate can be bypassed in non-interactive flows

security_findings.action: Implement output scrubbing before write (credential/token patterns and configured secret keys), and add regression tests that fail when known secret fixtures appear in offload/log files.
security_findings.risk: Journey C mandates offloading noisy command output to `.offload/<id>.txt` and structured logs, but no masking policy is defined. Tokens, credentials, or private env values may be persisted in plaintext artifacts.
security_findings.title: Offload/log pipeline lacks secret redaction requirements

security_findings.action: Create artifact directories/files with least-privilege permissions (`0700` dirs, `0600` files) and add automated checks for permission mode on creation.
security_findings.risk: The feature is local-only, but no requirement sets restrictive permissions for `.offload` and `logs/` artifacts. On shared machines, other local users could read sensitive workflow data.
security_findings.title: Artifact file permissions are unspecified

product_findings.action: Define measurable acceptance checks for default worktree count, naming convention, branch names, and required CLI success/summary output so users can verify outcomes deterministically.
product_findings.risk: The spec still uses generic success language and a placeholder metric (`{feature['outcome']}`), so completion can be claimed without proving the user gets consistent worktree isolation behavior.
product_findings.title: Acceptance criteria are not verifiable for end-user outcomes

product_findings.action: Specify exact error text and immediate recovery actions for existing worktree, branch conflict, and missing preconditions, including explicit rerun-safety messaging.
product_findings.risk: Edge-case handling says 'Choose new name' but does not provide deterministic remediation steps or rerun guidance, which can leave users stuck or retrying unsafely.
product_findings.title: Failure recovery UX is underspecified for real user retries

product_findings.action: Enforce and test fail-closed workflow status/output on any non-zero `make ci` or pre-commit result, aligned with SEC-06-004 and SEC-06-005.
product_findings.risk: Execution logs show both passing and failing gate histories; without explicit fail-closed user-facing behavior, users may believe completion is allowed after failed checks.
product_findings.title: Validation gate behavior is ambiguous from a user perspective

product_findings.action: Reconcile task status, remove unresolved placeholder WI entries from active tracking, and provide one authoritative readiness summary for feature review.
product_findings.risk: `dev-tasks.md` shows core tasks as Not Started while execution logs show implemented attempts and a placeholder WI entry, reducing PO confidence in workflow state.
product_findings.title: Readiness signals are inconsistent across feature artifacts

product_findings.action: Require explicit human validation sign-off for prompt clarity, handoff/stage wording, and recovery instructions before feature completion.
product_findings.risk: Automated tests alone cannot confirm that gate prompts, stage labels, and next-step instructions are clear for the Developer/PO user flow.
product_findings.title: Human usability sign-off is missing for CLI prompts and stage clarity

security_findings.action: Enforce a strict allowlist (for example `^[a-z0-9-]+$`) for feature/agent tokens, reject anything else, and execute git commands with fully quoted arguments and `--` separators (no eval/string-built command execution).
security_findings.risk: The spec requires a naming convention but does not define an allowed-character policy for feature/agent inputs used by CLI scripts. Without strict validation, crafted values can break shell safety or create unsafe git refs.
security_findings.title: Unsanitized worktree/branch input can enable command or ref-name injection

security_findings.action: Before create/reuse/remove, canonicalize paths, require they stay under the approved parent directory, reject symlinks, and verify target is a valid git worktree owned by this repo.
security_findings.risk: The documented naming pattern `../<repo>-<feature>-<agent>` and cleanup behavior create a boundary risk if paths are reused or symlinked. Current docs only mention "worktree exists" handling, not canonical path enforcement.
security_findings.title: Worktree path traversal/symlink escape not fail-closed

security_findings.action: Parse manifest with strict schema, verify each entry against `git worktree list --porcelain`, ignore/reject out-of-policy entries, and store manifest with restrictive permissions.
security_findings.risk: Execution logs mention manifest tracking plus auto-collection/cleanup, but no control is specified to treat manifest content as untrusted. A tampered manifest could redirect cleanup/collection to unintended paths or refs.
security_findings.title: Manifest-driven auto-collection/cleanup lacks integrity validation

security_findings.action: Enforce fail-closed completion: block feature completion on any non-zero `make ci`/pre-commit result and require a clean rerun before completion status can advance.
security_findings.risk: WI-20260204-02 records `make ci` failure (PermissionError) during execution, showing a path where required validation can be incomplete. This weakens guardrails that should prevent unsafe completion.
security_findings.title: Security gate can fail open when CI/pre-commit errors occur

security_findings.action: Add negative tests that assert hard failure for invalid names, path escapes, symlink reuse, and manifest mismatch; make these tests mandatory in `make test`/`make ci`.
security_findings.risk: Current test scenarios cover happy path and a generic missing-precondition case, but do not validate malicious names, branch conflict abuse, symlinked existing worktrees, or manifest tampering.
security_findings.title: Missing abuse-case tests for naming/conflict/symlink scenarios

product_findings.action: Fix the branch-gate path and `.codex/skills/readme-sync/SKILL.md` permission failure, rerun `make feature F=07` and `make ci`, and record PASS evidence in validation logs before marking complete.
product_findings.risk: Feature completion is being assessed while `make feature F=07` and `make ci` are failing, which undermines confidence that anti-cheat behavior and guardrails actually protect the user workflow.
product_findings.title: Required release gates are failing, so user-facing quality is unproven

product_findings.action: Add executable behavior tests using multiple fixture variations per critical path, invariant assertions across variants, and explicit failure when outputs are hardcoded regardless of wording.
product_findings.risk: Current checks can pass by matching wording (for example, 'multiple fixtures' and 'seeded randomness') while still allowing hardcoded or non-general behavior, reducing end-user trust in results.
product_findings.title: Anti-cheat acceptance is phrase-based instead of behavior-based

product_findings.action: Add tests that run identical seeds multiple times and assert identical outcomes, plus a negative test where unseeded paths fail with explicit retry guidance.
product_findings.risk: Without repeated-seed runtime checks and negative tests for unseeded execution, users can still experience flaky outcomes and unclear retry confidence.
product_findings.title: Determinism promise is not validated at runtime

product_findings.action: Add a guard/test for no network egress on F-07 workflow paths and log validation evidence in `docs/03-logs/validation-log.md`.
product_findings.risk: The feature promises no remote transfer, but no explicit automated proof is recorded; accidental network egress would violate user expectations and trust.
product_findings.title: Local-only operation claim lacks validation evidence

product_findings.action: PO must explicitly decide whether F-07 is archival-only or still acceptance-active, map evidence to the authoritative feature, and record sign-off decision.
product_findings.risk: Development/testing may optimize or close the wrong artifact, and end-user validation can be signed off against outdated scope.
product_findings.title: Acceptance authority is ambiguous because F-07 is marked shipped but superseded by F-08

security_findings.action: Fix the branch-gate execution path and the `.codex/skills/readme-sync/SKILL.md` permission error, then rerun `make feature F=07` and `make ci` and record PASS evidence in validation logs before completion.
security_findings.risk: Feature completion is being evaluated with failed gates (`make feature F=07` and `make ci`), so anti-cheat enforcement and pre-commit protections can be bypassed without a verified fail-closed result.
security_findings.title: Required security-relevant gates are failing

security_findings.action: Add executable anti-cheat tests that assert real behavior: multiple fixture-driven assertions per critical path, invariant checks across fixture variation, and failure on hardcoded outputs independent of wording.
security_findings.risk: Current tests and patch notes show enforcement around explicit wording (e.g., 'multiple fixtures', 'seeded randomness'), which can be satisfied textually while still shipping hardcoded or non-invariant behavior.
security_findings.title: Anti-cheat control is currently phrase-based, not behavior-verified

security_findings.action: Add deterministic test cases that run the same seed multiple times and assert identical outcomes; add a negative test that unseeded paths fail with explicit retry guidance.
security_findings.risk: Edge case coverage claims seeded randomness, but evidence is limited to policy/wording checks; flaky or nondeterministic tests may still pass review and mask regressions.
security_findings.title: Seeded-randomness requirement lacks runtime determinism proof

security_findings.action: Add a test or execution guard for F-07 workflow paths that asserts no network egress is required/used, and log the validation result in `docs/03-logs/validation-log.md`.
security_findings.risk: The feature spec declares local-only operation, but no explicit automated validation is recorded; accidental network egress during workflow execution could leak repo context.
security_findings.title: Local-only/no-remote-transfer security requirement is undocumented in validation evidence

product_findings.action: Enforce a fail-closed completion gate: require recorded `make ci` pass evidence before status can be set to Complete.
product_findings.risk: WI-20260205-02 shows outcome pass/complete while `make ci` was not run, so users can receive a 'done' signal without full anti-cheat and integration validation.
product_findings.title: Completion can be marked without final CI proof

product_findings.action: Either hard-fail `pc-ticket` with migration guidance or force strict delegation to the exact validated gate path with equivalent evidence output.
product_findings.risk: Restoring `pc-ticket` as a stub can let users follow a weaker or unclear execution path, reducing confidence that anti-cheat gates were actually applied.
product_findings.title: `pc-ticket` restoration creates user path ambiguity

product_findings.action: Add generated or mutated fixture coverage plus metamorphic/invariant checks per critical path and require them in CI.
product_findings.risk: Multiple static fixtures and invariants alone may still allow memorized/hardcoded behavior to pass, weakening user trust in test quality.
product_findings.title: Current anti-cheat acceptance can still be gamed

product_findings.action: Add automated anti-egress checks for anti-cheat workflows and fail tests on any outbound network attempt.
product_findings.risk: Without outbound network denial/monitoring tests, workflows may accidentally call remote services, violating local-only expectations and reproducibility.
product_findings.title: Local-only promise is not enforced in automated checks

product_findings.action: Route final PO/security review through human validation and require explicit sign-off before completion status is retained.
product_findings.risk: Feature is marked Complete while DoD item 'Code is reviewed and merged' remains unchecked, leaving product acceptance accountability unresolved.
product_findings.title: Human sign-off gate is incomplete

product_findings.action: Replace placeholders with explicit measurable outcomes and map each to a concrete validation artifact.
product_findings.risk: The metric table still contains a placeholder (`{feature['outcome']}`), so users cannot verify outcome quality consistently across runs.
product_findings.title: Success metrics are partially non-actionable

security_findings.action: Require `make ci` evidence before feature completion and fail closed when the command is missing or failing.
security_findings.risk: In WI-20260205-02, `make ci` is explicitly marked as not run while outcome is pass/complete. This leaves anti-cheat controls and integration checks unverified and allows fail-open completion.
security_findings.title: Final fail-closed CI gate was skipped

security_findings.action: Make `pc-ticket` either hard-fail with migration guidance or delegate to the exact same validated gate path with explicit proof output.
security_findings.risk: Patch notes state `pc-ticket` was restored as a stub; if this path does not strictly delegate to hardened anti-cheat checks, users can bypass enforcement in `pc-feature`/allowed-tests flow.
security_findings.title: Restored `pc-ticket` stub creates potential gate-bypass path

security_findings.action: Add invariant/metamorphic or generated-fixture tests for each critical path and require at least one non-static fixture source in CI.
security_findings.risk: The feature requires multiple fixtures, but provided docs do not require fixture mutation/generation. A hardcoded implementation can still pass by memorizing known fixture sets.
security_findings.title: Current anti-cheat spec can still be beaten by fixture memorization

security_findings.action: Add automated tests that block/monitor outbound network access during anti-cheat workflows and fail on any egress.
security_findings.risk: Spec says local-only with no remote transfer, but test evidence shown does not include a network-egress denial check. Outbound calls could leak data or fetch answers.
security_findings.title: Local-only security claim is not enforced by tests

security_findings.action: Require explicit human security/PO validation of anti-cheat gate behavior before marking feature complete.
security_findings.risk: DoD shows `Code is reviewed and merged` unchecked while feature status is Complete, creating a security sign-off gap for gate logic changes.
security_findings.title: Human security review gate is incomplete

product_findings.action: Resolve the permission blocker, rerun full make ci, and record passing evidence in validation logs before keeping status Done.
product_findings.risk: make ci is recorded as failed while the feature is marked complete, so users cannot trust deterministic gate outcomes or final quality status.
product_findings.title: Feature marked Done without full gate evidence

product_findings.action: Enforce fail-closed behavior for missing/unwritable log paths and emit clear remediation plus rerun-safety messaging.
product_findings.risk: If required logs cannot be created/appended, execution may proceed without audit trails, breaking the core user promise of debuggable, deterministic runs.
product_findings.title: Traceability can fail open when logs are unavailable

product_findings.action: Validate metadata with a strict allowlist, enforce canonical paths under logs/, reject/escape control characters, and add negative tests.
product_findings.risk: Unsanitized metadata can cause path traversal or forged log lines, making user-facing logs unreliable for debugging and review.
product_findings.title: Structured log trust can be broken by unsafe metadata handling

product_findings.action: Implement redaction for sensitive patterns, add regression tests with synthetic secrets, and document the redaction policy/limits.
product_findings.risk: CI/tests/precommit logs can capture secrets, creating end-user security and cleanup risk in local and CI artifacts.
product_findings.title: Sensitive output redaction is not guaranteed

product_findings.action: Add automated validation covering all required run types and record concrete log-path/prefix evidence in feature validation logs.
product_findings.risk: User expectations require logs for CI, tests, precommit, and feature runs; current validation evidence does not clearly prove all surfaces end-to-end.
product_findings.title: Acceptance evidence is incomplete across all required run surfaces

security_findings.action: In the runner/log helper, validate `work_item_id`, `agent_name`, `step`, and `run_id` against a strict allowlist (e.g., `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`), resolve canonical paths, and hard-fail if the target is outside `logs/`.
security_findings.risk: The feature requires metadata-driven log paths (`logs/<WI>/<step>.log`) but the provided docs do not define path sanitization. Malformed `work_item_id` or `step` values can escape `logs/` and overwrite arbitrary files.
security_findings.title: Path traversal risk in `logs/<WI>/<step>.log` construction

security_findings.action: Escape or reject control characters in all metadata fields and enforce one-event-per-line output (prefer JSONL with encoded fields). Add tests that inject newline/tab/ANSI characters and verify safe output.
security_findings.risk: Required prefix format (`[WI-...][agent][step]`) is vulnerable if metadata contains newlines/control characters; attackers can spoof entries, break parsers, or hide actions in tail/debug workflows.
security_findings.title: Log forging/injection via unescaped metadata fields

security_findings.action: Implement output redaction before write (token/header/password patterns), add regression tests with synthetic secrets, and document a denylist/allowlist policy for logged fields.
security_findings.risk: Feature scope logs CI/tests/precommit output, which often contains secrets or tokens. No redaction control is specified in feature docs, creating credential leakage risk in local/CI artifacts.
security_findings.title: Sensitive data exposure in structured command logs

security_findings.action: Require non-zero exit when required step logs cannot be created/appended, and add automated tests for missing/unwritable `logs/<WI>` paths.
security_findings.risk: Edge case `logs directory missing or not writable` is listed, but docs do not require fail-closed behavior. Execution may continue without audit logs, defeating traceability controls.
security_findings.title: Fail-open behavior for unwritable log directory is not enforced

security_findings.action: Resolve the permission issue and rerun full `make ci`; do not finalize feature status until the gate passes with evidence recorded in validation logs.
security_findings.risk: Execution log records `make ci` failure (permission error) while feature is marked Done. This leaves security-relevant checks unproven in the full gate path.
security_findings.title: Security gate evidence incomplete before feature completion

product_findings.action: Snapshot the pre-hook staged set (`git diff --cached --name-only -z`), restage only that set (or its autofix-touched subset), and fail if out-of-scope tracked files changed.
product_findings.risk: Using broad restage behavior after autofix can silently add unrelated tracked edits, breaking user trust and making commits unpredictable.
product_findings.title: Restaging scope can include unrelated user work

product_findings.action: Hard-pin vanilla Codex config/env in precommit and exit non-zero if vanilla mode cannot be enforced; add a regression check that rejects Serena-enabled execution.
product_findings.risk: If precommit can fall back to non-vanilla config, behavior diverges from spec and can enable unintended MCP integrations.
product_findings.title: Vanilla precommit mode is not fail-closed

product_findings.action: Propagate non-zero exit codes end-to-end and add negative-path automated tests that inject autofix failure and assert commit/CI is blocked.
product_findings.risk: If unified autofix errors do not reliably propagate, commits/CI can proceed with partially fixed or unchecked code.
product_findings.title: Autofix failure path may fail open

product_findings.action: Define and test a deterministic no-staged-files outcome (clear message, no staging changes, correct exit code).
product_findings.risk: Without explicit no-op behavior and messaging, users cannot tell whether nothing needed fixing or the hook skipped work incorrectly.
product_findings.title: No-staged-files behavior is under-specified for users

product_findings.action: Use NUL-delimited git output and array-safe shell handling; add regression tests with problematic filenames.
product_findings.risk: Whitespace/newline/special-character paths can be misparsed, causing wrong files to be processed or staged.
product_findings.title: Filename parsing robustness is not guaranteed

product_findings.action: Run PO validation on success/failure/no-op scenarios and record explicit sign-off for message clarity and remediation guidance.
product_findings.risk: Even with technical correctness, unclear hook output can cause incorrect user decisions during commit flow.
product_findings.title: Human validation of CLI workflow clarity is missing

security_findings.action: In the unified autofix script, snapshot the pre-hook staged path set (`git diff --cached --name-only -z`), restage only that set (or its autofix-touched subset), and hard-fail if autofix changed tracked files outside scope.
security_findings.risk: The feature spec already flags "Unexpected staging of unrelated files"; using `git add -u` after autofix can silently include unrelated edits in the commit.
security_findings.title: Unscoped `git add -u` can stage unrelated tracked changes

security_findings.action: Hard-pin vanilla config/env in `tools/pc-precommit` and fail immediately if vanilla mode cannot be applied; add a regression check that rejects Serena-enabled execution.
security_findings.risk: Requirement 3 mandates vanilla config (no Serena MCP), but acceptance criteria do not enforce a guard; hook execution could fall back to user/global config and enable external MCP connectors.
security_findings.title: Vanilla Codex mode is required but not fail-closed

security_findings.action: Propagate non-zero exit codes from unified autofix through precommit and CI, and add a negative-path automated test that injects autofix failure and asserts commit/CI is blocked.
security_findings.risk: Edge case only requires a clear error message; without explicit non-zero propagation, precommit/CI can fail open and allow partially fixed or unchecked code.
security_findings.title: Autofix failure path is not explicitly commit-blocking

security_findings.action: Use NUL-delimited git output (`-z`) and strict quoted/array-safe shell handling, plus a regression test with problematic filenames.
security_findings.risk: If staged-file handling is whitespace/shell-split based, crafted filenames (spaces/newlines/globs) can be misparsed, causing unintended file processing or staging.
security_findings.title: Filename/path parsing safety is unspecified

product_findings.action: Add explicit acceptance and implementation behavior to hard-fail when match count is 0 or >1, with deterministic remediation text and guaranteed no mutation before resolution.
product_findings.risk: If zero or multiple worktrees match, users can run patch/test in the wrong checkout or face unclear failure behavior.
product_findings.title: Fail-closed worktree selection is not an explicit user acceptance condition

product_findings.action: Define and implement consistent deprecated-file handling in docs and CLI output: ignore legacy file, warn clearly, and provide the next action.
product_findings.risk: Users with existing repos may assume the legacy file is still authoritative, causing workflow confusion and inconsistent outcomes.
product_findings.title: Legacy `feature-worktrees.json` deprecation UX is undefined

product_findings.action: Add automated negative tests that assert non-zero exit, no file mutation, and actionable remediation messaging for zero/multiple worktrees, symlink path rejection, and legacy file presence.
product_findings.risk: Regressions in ambiguous/missing/symlink/legacy states can silently return, breaking trust and increasing manual recovery effort.
product_findings.title: Recovery behavior is not acceptance-tested from the user perspective

product_findings.action: Add a migration section to process docs covering detection of extra worktrees, canonical selection/remediation, legacy cleanup expectations, and rerun-safe verification.
product_findings.risk: Current users may not know how to move from legacy tracking to the single-worktree model, leading to blocked or inconsistent executions.
product_findings.title: Migration path for existing repositories is under-specified

product_findings.action: Require PO/end-user sign-off in human validation using at least one legacy scenario (legacy file present and multiple worktrees) to confirm instructions are understandable and actionable.
product_findings.risk: Implementation can pass technical checks while still leaving end-user instructions unclear in real legacy scenarios.
product_findings.title: No required human validation of workflow clarity after migration

security_findings.action: Implement deterministic worktree resolution that hard-fails when match count is 0 or >1, with explicit remediation output before any patch/test step proceeds.
security_findings.risk: The spec lists the edge case "Multiple worktrees exist for a feature", but acceptance only says to remove `feature-worktrees.json`. Without an enforced stop when candidate worktrees != 1, patch/test can run in the wrong checkout.
security_findings.title: Single-worktree invariant is not fail-closed

security_findings.action: Canonicalize with `realpath`, reject symlinks/untrusted paths, and enforce allowed root-prefix checks before any read/write or command execution against a resolved worktree path.
security_findings.risk: Moving from explicit JSON tracking to filesystem discovery introduces path/symlink abuse risk if canonical-path validation is not enforced, allowing operations outside the intended repo/worktree root.
security_findings.title: Path-boundary controls are missing after metadata removal

security_findings.action: Remove all runtime reads/writes of `feature-worktrees.json`, add explicit deprecated-file handling (ignore + warning), and fail CI if executable code references the file.
security_findings.risk: The edge case "Legacy files still present" is documented, but no required control states runtime must ignore/deprecate the file. Residual code paths could still consume stale or attacker-modified JSON.
security_findings.title: Legacy `feature-worktrees.json` is an unneutralized trust input

security_findings.action: Add automated negative tests for: multiple matching worktrees, zero matching worktrees, legacy file present, and symlinked candidate path; require non-zero exit and no file mutation.
security_findings.risk: Current tasks do not require tests that prove fail-closed behavior for multi-worktree and legacy-file scenarios, so unsafe fallback behavior can regress silently.
security_findings.title: No negative security regression tests for ambiguous worktree states

product_findings.action: Complete and record automated validation for idempotent reruns, no-delete guarantees, duplicate prevention, done-skip determinism, and update-only-missing-sections; attach results in validation/report logs before completion.
product_findings.risk: Feature claims (add-only, no-delete, done-skip, update-in-place) are not backed by completed execution/test/report evidence, so users could trust unsafe behavior and lose backlog integrity.
product_findings.title: Acceptance contract is marked Done without validation evidence

product_findings.action: Implement and test deterministic per-feature reason codes for created/updated/skipped plus recovery-safe messaging (resumed/skipped/repaired/newly executed and immediate remediation when blocked).
product_findings.risk: Users need deterministic reasons and recovery guidance per item; without tested summary semantics, reruns after interruptions can become guesswork and increase accidental edits.
product_findings.title: Run summary does not yet prove recovery-grade workflow clarity

product_findings.action: Require human confirmation for drift cases with an explicit mapping table and selected target before proceeding.
product_findings.risk: When PRD labels drift from existing folder slugs, silent or automatic mapping can update the wrong feature and break user trust in incremental updates.
product_findings.title: Slug/index drift lacks explicit human decision gate

product_findings.action: Route any override of malformed/missing Status to explicit PO sign-off and log the approval rationale before any update is allowed.
product_findings.risk: Security requires fail-closed parsing, but without a documented human override path, users may apply ad-hoc workarounds that produce inconsistent feature states.
product_findings.title: Malformed/missing Status handling needs human override governance

product_findings.action: Define concrete section-level invariants and add automated diff-based tests showing what must remain unchanged vs what may be filled in.
product_findings.risk: Ambiguous edit scope can cause unexpected content changes even when no destructive intent exists.
product_findings.title: ‘Update only missing/incomplete sections’ is not acceptance-testable yet

security_findings.action: Enforce strict slug allowlist, reject path separators/dot segments/control chars, resolve realpath for every target, and hard-fail if target is not under docs/02-features before any read/write.
security_findings.risk: The feature requires parsing PRD feature labels and creating folders, but the docs do not require path normalization/validation. A crafted label/slug (e.g., with ../ or absolute paths) could make patching write outside docs/02-features.
security_findings.title: PRD-derived folder names are not constrained to a safe write root

security_findings.action: Use lstat-based symlink detection on feature directories and managed files, refuse symlink targets, and fail-closed with explicit reporting; do not follow symlinks during update operations.
security_findings.risk: The feature updates existing folders/files in place, but no control requires symlink checks. A symlinked feature folder or dev-tasks.md could redirect writes to unintended files.
security_findings.title: In-place update flow lacks symlink boundary protection

security_findings.action: Implement strict status parsing and fail-closed behavior for missing/invalid Status (skip + explicit reason) unless an explicit human override path is invoked.
security_findings.risk: Edge cases explicitly include malformed/missing Status, and risks mention loose parsing. If ambiguous status defaults to updatable, Done content can be modified unintentionally, breaking integrity guarantees.
security_findings.title: Malformed or missing Status parsing can fail open

security_findings.action: Add automated tests for traversal attempts, absolute-path inputs, symlinked feature paths/files, and malformed-status fail-closed behavior; require these tests to pass before feature completion.
security_findings.risk: Current test expectations cover idempotency/no-delete but do not explicitly require traversal/symlink abuse cases, so boundary regressions may ship undetected.
security_findings.title: Security boundary tests are missing from required validation set

product_findings.action: Implement fixed role/task filename allowlists, canonicalize resolved paths, enforce prompt-root confinement, and fail closed on unknown identifiers with clear remediation text.
product_findings.risk: If role/task identifiers are not strictly allowlisted and path-confined, users can get inconsistent role behavior and non-deterministic runs, breaking trust in the workflow.
product_findings.title: Prompt loader can select unintended files

product_findings.action: Enforce explicit `Awaiting PO Approval` state and block all downstream stages until recorded human approval is present.
product_findings.risk: If conflict handling does not hard-stop at approval gates, patch/test can continue without PO authorization, violating user expectations for safety and control.
product_findings.title: HIGH-risk conflict path is not proven fail-closed

product_findings.action: Add automated one-to-one inventory and content parity tests between `prompts/` and `tools/templates/prompts/`, failing on any mismatch.
product_findings.risk: Template reapply can silently reintroduce stale prompt wording, causing role handoff regressions and avoidable replan loops for end users.
product_findings.title: Prompt/template drift is not gated by mandatory parity tests

product_findings.action: Run and record the gate-focused tests for all required paths and update validation logs with concrete pass/fail evidence.
product_findings.risk: Approve/block/retry/conflict/missing-prompt behavior is not evidenced as executed, so completion quality and user-facing reliability remain unverified.
product_findings.title: Acceptance-critical gate behavior lacks test evidence

product_findings.action: Route to PO human-validation with a scripted walkthrough of approve, block/retry, conflict, and missing-prompt scenarios; require explicit sign-off or requested copy fixes.
product_findings.risk: Without human validation of blocked/conflict/error messaging, users may not know next actions, increasing failed reruns and workflow friction.
product_findings.title: User-facing gate and remediation wording lacks explicit PO sign-off

security_findings.action: In `tools/pc-feature`, map role/task identifiers to a fixed allowlist of filenames, canonicalize resolved paths, enforce they stay under the prompt root, and fail closed on unknown identifiers with remediation text.
security_findings.risk: Feature requirements require file-based prompt loading with task fallback, but the provided spec/tasks do not require a strict allowlist + path confinement check. Without this, a crafted role/task key could resolve outside `prompts/` and load unintended files.
security_findings.title: Prompt loader path confinement is not explicitly enforced

security_findings.action: Implement explicit conflict behavior that sets `Awaiting PO Approval` and blocks downstream patch/test stages until a recorded human approval is present.
security_findings.risk: Edge Case 2 calls out reviewer guidance vs HIGH-risk policy conflicts, but acceptance criteria do not explicitly require a hard halt state. A non-fail-closed conflict path can allow work to continue without required PO approval.
security_findings.title: Plan Reviewer conflict handling is not guaranteed to fail-closed

security_findings.action: Add automated tests that enforce one-to-one inventory and content parity between `prompts/` and `tools/templates/prompts/`; fail test on any mismatch.
security_findings.risk: Requirement 3 and Edge Case 3 require template sync, but provided materials do not show a mandatory fail-closed test gate for prompt parity. Drift can reintroduce weaker or outdated prompts during bootstrap/template sync.
security_findings.title: Prompt/template drift control is not enforced by a mandatory automated parity test

security_findings.action: Run and record the gate-focused tests for approve, block/retry, policy conflict, and missing prompt handling before feature completion; update validation logs with concrete pass/fail evidence.
security_findings.risk: Dev tasks and execution log show pending test sections (`Test Results: (pending)`, `Final Report: No runs yet`). Missing evidence means approve/block/conflict and missing-prompt fail-fast controls are unverified.
security_findings.title: Security-critical gate tests are not evidenced as completed

product_findings.action: Add mandatory pre-write redaction, sanitization, and length limiting with fail-closed behavior if safety processing cannot complete.
product_findings.risk: Fail/stall summaries can leak secrets or include unsafe/garbled content, which undermines trust in `docs/possible-improvements.md` and creates review friction for the Developer/PO.
product_findings.title: Proposal content safety is not enforced before writing to user-facing docs

product_findings.action: Harden dedup with collision-safe matching (canonical hash + raw-evidence comparison) and record explicit collision rationale instead of silent skip/merge.
product_findings.risk: Current signature strategy can over-merge incidents, hiding separate root causes and reducing the learning loop’s value.
product_findings.title: Dedup logic can suppress distinct user-impacting failures

product_findings.action: Add automated tests for secret-bearing summaries, markdown/control-character payloads, and dedup near-collision cases; make these tests required for completion.
product_findings.risk: Without malicious and near-collision fixtures, regressions in redaction, sanitization, and dedup integrity can ship while core acceptance still appears green.
product_findings.title: Acceptance quality lacks adversarial test coverage

product_findings.action: Enforce deterministic status consistency checks across feature logs/reports and update generated artifacts so completion evidence is unambiguous.
product_findings.risk: Feature artifacts show mixed completion signals (e.g., completed status with pending sections), which weakens workflow clarity and approval confidence.
product_findings.title: Workflow evidence appears internally inconsistent

product_findings.action: Add a human validation checklist for proposal approval covering usefulness, clarity, duplicate rationale, and safety review before status changes from `Proposed`.
product_findings.risk: Approvals may be inconsistent if reviewers are not required to verify user-value quality (clear problem statement, actionable improvement, and safe content).
product_findings.title: Human approval criteria are not explicit enough for proposal quality

security_findings.action: Add a mandatory redaction pass before proposal write (credential/secret patterns + high-entropy token heuristics), replace matches with `[REDACTED]`, and fail-closed if redaction cannot safely process payload.
security_findings.risk: Feature docs require writing fail/stall context into `docs/possible-improvements.md`, but no requirement/test enforces masking of tokens, keys, passwords, or PII from logs; sensitive data can be committed to git.
security_findings.title: Failure summaries are persisted without secret redaction controls

security_findings.action: Normalize proposal fields to safe plaintext (strip control/ANSI chars, escape markdown-sensitive characters where needed), enforce maximum field lengths, and append a truncated note with log pointer.
security_findings.risk: Failure text from execution context can include ANSI/control bytes or crafted markdown content; without sanitization/length limits this can poison docs rendering, mislead reviewers, and create oversized proposal entries.
security_findings.title: Untrusted log content is not constrained before markdown insertion

security_findings.action: Harden dedup with canonical hashing of raw summary + normalized key, and require collision-safe behavior (append separate evidence/collision note instead of silent skip when raw payloads differ).
security_findings.risk: Current signature (`work item + step + normalized summary`, excluding agent) can over-merge distinct failures, allowing security-relevant incidents to be suppressed as duplicates.
security_findings.title: Dedup signature is collision-prone for incident integrity

security_findings.action: Add automated tests with malicious fixtures: secret-bearing summaries, control-character/markdown payloads, and near-collision dedup inputs; gate completion on these passing.
security_findings.risk: Defined tests cover happy-path fail/stall/dedup/success only; regressions in redaction, sanitization, and collision handling can ship undetected.
security_findings.title: Security abuse cases are missing from automated tests

security_findings.action: Add a human-validation checklist item requiring verification that proposal entries contain no secrets and no unsafe execution instructions before `Approved`.
security_findings.risk: Docs specify `Proposed` human gating but no explicit validation checklist for sensitive-data leakage or unsafe proposal text, increasing approval inconsistency.
security_findings.title: Human gate lacks explicit security review criteria

product_findings.action: Enforce fail-closed destination validation to `docs/03-logs/compacted/` only, fail execution on drift, and regenerate/migrate compact outputs to the required path.
product_findings.risk: Reporter iterations show compacted artifacts repeatedly written outside `docs/03-logs/compacted/`, so users cannot trust where to find the canonical compact view.
product_findings.title: Compaction output path is not reliable for users

product_findings.action: Reinstate and enforce automated suites for offload index, retention, and log compaction as mandatory completion gates.
product_findings.risk: Current Allowed Tests emphasize `tests.test_pc_feature`, so offload index/retention/compaction regressions can slip through while feature-level user value is marked complete.
product_findings.title: Acceptance quality is unproven by current test gate

product_findings.action: Add reference-aware purge protection by default, require explicit destructive override, and log override actions immutably.
product_findings.risk: If purge removes artifacts still referenced by active work items, users lose debugging context and incident traceability.
product_findings.title: Retention flow can delete actively referenced evidence

product_findings.action: Implement deterministic command scrubbing/masking before index write, scrub existing indexed entries, and add regression tests.
product_findings.risk: Persisting unsanitized command metadata can leak secrets in index/log artifacts, creating user trust and safety risk.
product_findings.title: Raw command capture risks exposing sensitive inputs

product_findings.action: Run human review on sampled compacted entries across decision/implementation/validation logs and record explicit sign-off against acceptance criteria.
product_findings.risk: Automated checks alone do not prove summaries preserve rationale, chronology, and evidence quality needed for Developer/PO decision-making.
product_findings.title: Compacted-log usefulness lacks explicit PO validation

product_findings.action: Add deterministic user-facing remediation guidance (refresh/rebuild flow) for stale reference and missing artifact cases.
product_findings.risk: When source sections shift or referenced artifacts are missing, users may not know the safe remediation path.
product_findings.title: Recovery guidance for stale/missing compact references is unclear

security_findings.action: Implement deterministic command scrubbing before index write (secret-pattern masking, sensitive-flag masking, length caps), scrub existing index entries, and add regression tests proving secret-like inputs are never persisted in cleartext.
security_findings.risk: Requirement 1 requires persisting full `command` metadata, but no redaction control is defined in the provided spec/tasks. Secrets passed via CLI args can be stored in `.offload/index.jsonl` and propagated into logs.
security_findings.title: Unredacted command capture in offload index

security_findings.action: Add reference-aware purge protection that blocks deletion of referenced IDs by default, require explicit override for destructive purge, and emit immutable audit log entries for overrides.
security_findings.risk: Edge Case 2 explicitly states purge may remove artifacts still referenced by active work items, but no fail-closed safeguard is specified. This can destroy forensic evidence and undermine incident reconstruction.
security_findings.title: Purge can delete evidence referenced by active work items

security_findings.action: Reinstate and enforce automated suites covering `tests/test_offload_index.py`, `tests/test_offload_retention.py`, and `tests/test_log_compaction.py`; fail workflow if these suites are omitted or skipped.
security_findings.risk: The current Allowed Tests list in dev-tasks is narrowed to `tests.test_pc_feature`, so offload index/retention/compaction controls can regress without automated detection.
security_findings.title: Security-critical invariants are not enforced by current allowed test gate

security_findings.action: Enforce strict output-path validation (only `docs/03-logs/compacted/` allowed), fail execution on path drift, and add tests asserting destination invariants.
security_findings.risk: Iteration logs show compacted artifacts were repeatedly written outside required `docs/03-logs/compacted/`. Uncontrolled output paths create shadow audit records and weaken traceability integrity.
security_findings.title: Compaction destination integrity is not fail-closed

product_findings.action: Implement a fixed warning template that always includes earlier incomplete feature IDs/statuses, remediation path, and next eligible feature/action; add deterministic output tests.
product_findings.risk: If warning copy is inconsistent or incomplete, users cannot recover quickly and may continue out-of-order execution, reducing trust in the governance signal.
product_findings.title: Sequencing warning lacks deterministic recovery contract

product_findings.action: Define bounded mining thresholds (minimum repeats, source diversity, dedupe/cooldown) and enforce them with tests for noisy vs high-signal datasets.
product_findings.risk: Without explicit repeat/signal thresholds and deduping, low-value proposals will create review fatigue and hide genuinely useful skills.
product_findings.title: Skill-mining quality thresholds are under-specified

product_findings.action: Add regression coverage proving existing hard-fail gates remain non-zero while sequencing warnings stay advisory-only (aligned with SEC-16-003).
product_findings.risk: Users may assume hard commit protections still apply even if exit-code behavior regresses, causing unsafe commits.
product_findings.title: Soft-warning change may weaken perceived commit protection

product_findings.action: Require PO/end-user validation for first proposal batch using a checklist (usefulness, duplication, maintenance cost, security/redaction evidence) with explicit approve/reject outcomes logged.
product_findings.risk: If approval criteria are implicit, proposal acceptance will be inconsistent and end-user value will drift.
product_findings.title: Human approval gate for mined proposals is not operationalized

product_findings.action: Run human spot checks on warning clarity for single-feature and multi-feature commits and record comprehension feedback.
product_findings.risk: Technically correct warnings may still be hard to act on under time pressure, reducing adherence.
product_findings.title: Warning usability is not yet validated in real commit scenarios

security_findings.action: Implement fail-closed secret handling in miner output: detect credentials (token/key/password patterns + high-entropy strings), redact values, and store only minimal references (path + line/offset/hash) instead of raw secret-bearing text.
security_findings.risk: The feature explicitly mines `prompts/`, `logs/`, and `.offload/` and writes evidence references, but no redaction rule is defined; secrets/tokens in those sources can be committed to `docs/possible-improvements.md` and leaked via git history.
security_findings.title: Sensitive data can be copied into skill proposals

security_findings.action: Constrain mining to an allowlisted repo-relative set after `realpath` validation, reject paths outside repo root, do not follow symlinks, skip binary files, and cap file size/line length before parsing.
security_findings.risk: Input sources are defined as directories, but no canonical path/symlink policy is specified; a symlink or traversal path could cause reading files outside the repo (for example local SSH/config secrets) and include them in proposals.
security_findings.title: Repository-boundary enforcement is missing for mined inputs

security_findings.action: Add regression tests proving existing hard-fail gates still return non-zero while sequencing warnings remain advisory-only; enforce additive warning behavior only.
security_findings.risk: This feature adds non-blocking precommit behavior; without explicit regression tests, exit-code changes can unintentionally weaken existing fail-closed commit checks in the workflow.
security_findings.title: Soft-warning implementation could accidentally bypass hard commit controls

security_findings.action: On parse ambiguity or missing status, emit deterministic `unknown status` warnings with affected feature IDs and remediation text; add tests for malformed, duplicate, and missing status fields.
security_findings.risk: Edge cases mention malformed `dev-tasks.md`, but no required fail-closed warning contract is defined; crafted/invalid status lines could evade out-of-order warnings.
security_findings.title: Malformed status parsing can silently suppress governance signal

security_findings.action: Normalize mined text before proposal generation: strip control characters, escape markdown where needed, and render evidence as plain text snippets.
security_findings.risk: Logs and offloaded outputs may contain ANSI/control sequences or malicious markdown that can spoof terminal/docs rendering and mislead reviewers.
security_findings.title: Control-character and markdown injection in mined evidence

product_findings.action: Require both Allowed Tests on every resumed and non-resumed run; hard-stop progression when either test is missing or non-zero; add regression proving resume cannot advance after docs-log test failure.
product_findings.risk: Run history shows resumed flow continued while `tests.test_docs_logs` failed or was skipped, so users can get unsafe continuation with false confidence.
product_findings.title: Resume path can pass with incomplete quality gates

product_findings.action: Implement deterministic non-interactive policy (fail closed unless explicit override), with TTY/non-TTY tests and explicit CLI messaging.
product_findings.risk: In non-TTY/CI contexts, undefined `prompt` handling can silently continue stale state or reset active WIP, causing user data/workflow loss.
product_findings.title: Non-interactive `prompt` behavior is ambiguous

product_findings.action: Centralize resume-state validation before routing; reject contradictory/malformed/missing-critical artifacts with clear remediation; add deterministic negative tests per contradiction class.
product_findings.risk: Users may be routed to the wrong step and skip required validation gates if contradictory/malformed artifact combinations are not centrally blocked.
product_findings.title: Contradictory artifact handling is not proven fail-closed

product_findings.action: Enforce required resume checkpoint fields in writer logic and docs-log tests, and block completion when required evidence is missing.
product_findings.risk: Missing Patch/Test/Reporter checkpoints reduce user ability to understand what resumed, what reran, and why completion is blocked.
product_findings.title: Resume audit trail completeness is inconsistent

product_findings.action: Run PO/end-user validation of resume prompts and summaries on interrupted-run scenarios; approve wording/defaults before release.
product_findings.risk: Even with technical fixes, unclear `auto`/`prompt`/`fresh` wording can lead users to destructive choices and perceived workflow unreliability.
product_findings.title: Risky resume-choice UX needs human sign-off

security_findings.action: Make both Allowed Tests mandatory for resumed and non-resumed paths; hard-fail execution when either test is missing or non-zero, and add a regression asserting resume cannot advance after docs-log contract failure.
security_findings.risk: Work-item history shows repeated `tests.test_docs_logs` failures/skips and `needs replan` outcomes while resume work continued, so fail-closed resume/traceability controls can be bypassed in practice.
security_findings.title: Required resume safety tests are not consistently enforced

security_findings.action: Define and implement deterministic non-interactive behavior now (recommended: `prompt` fails closed unless explicit override flag is provided) and cover TTY/non-TTY cases in tests.
security_findings.risk: The feature spec leaves an open question for `prompt` behavior; in CI/non-TTY contexts this can silently choose resume/fresh behavior, causing unintended reset of WIP or unsafe continuation.
security_findings.title: `prompt` mode is security-ambiguous in non-interactive runs

security_findings.action: Centralize resume-state validation before any role routing; reject contradictory/malformed/missing-critical artifact combinations with explicit remediation and add deterministic negative tests for each contradiction class.
security_findings.risk: Feature requirements demand fail-closed blocking on contradictory artifacts, but multiple execution blocks remain pending/needs-replan, so there is no reliable evidence the contradiction gate cannot be bypassed.
security_findings.title: Contradictory artifact handling lacks completed proof of enforcement

security_findings.action: Enforce required resume checkpoint/evidence fields in writer logic and docs-log tests, and block completion when any required field is missing.
security_findings.risk: Reporter failures explicitly cite missing Patch/Test/Reporter execution fields; incomplete logs weaken forensic traceability and commit-gate integrity for resumed runs.
security_findings.title: Resume audit trail completeness is not guaranteed

features.feature_title: Commit gated by completed ticket docs

product_findings.action: PO must choose and document a single policy (fail-closed only, or controlled override with approval artifact ID, reason, and audit logging) and update acceptance criteria before release.
product_findings.risk: The open override question can create either dead-end blocking during urgent fixes or informal bypasses, both of which reduce trust in the workflow and audit trail.
product_findings.title: Override policy is unresolved for real incident workflows

product_findings.action: Require machine-verifiable evidence (offload/log pointer + success status), block stale/forged pointers, and add negative automated tests for spoofed evidence.
product_findings.risk: Users can pass commit gating with fabricated 'Tests run' or report text, creating false confidence for reviewers and downstream handoffs.
product_findings.title: Gate checks presence of sections but not authenticity of evidence

product_findings.action: Add mandatory redaction and fail-closed secret detection before metadata write; include fixtures with injected secrets to prove masking/blocking.
product_findings.risk: Command metadata may capture tokens/credentials and commit them to history, creating direct user and operational risk.
product_findings.title: Auto-filled command metadata can leak secrets

product_findings.action: Enforce realpath-based repo-root allowlisting, reject symlink/.. escapes, and add regression tests for traversal and symlink scenarios.
product_findings.risk: Path traversal/symlink cases can evaluate unintended files, causing confusing gate outcomes and potential exposure beyond intended scope.
product_findings.title: Out-of-scope guard lacks canonical path and symlink safety

product_findings.action: Add CLI contract tests asserting deterministic remediation output includes missing field, expected location, and exact next step per failure mode.
product_findings.risk: Blocked users may receive inconsistent or non-actionable guidance, increasing retry loops and reducing workflow clarity.
product_findings.title: Remediation UX quality is not contract-tested

security_findings.action: Fail closed by default in code and protocol: disallow overrides unless a PO-approved override model is explicitly documented. If approved later, require explicit override flag, approval artifact ID, reason, and audit logging; add tests proving no silent bypass exists.
