security_findings.risk: The feature spec leaves emergency override behavior as an open question, which can introduce undocumented bypass paths that allow incomplete evidence to be committed.
security_findings.title: Commit-gate override policy is unresolved

security_findings.action: Add mandatory redaction and fail-closed checks for secret patterns and high-entropy credential-like values before writing metadata; add automated fixtures with injected secrets to verify masking/blocking.
security_findings.risk: The spec requires auto-filling deterministic command metadata but does not require secret redaction, so tokens/credentials in command lines can be committed to docs.
security_findings.title: Auto-filled command metadata can leak secrets into git history

security_findings.action: Require machine-verifiable evidence links (existing offload/log pointers with success exit code) for required sections; block on missing, stale, or mismatched artifacts; add negative tests for forged pointers.
security_findings.risk: Current acceptance/tests focus on missing/empty sections, allowing fabricated `Tests run` or final report text to satisfy the gate without real execution evidence.
security_findings.title: Gate validates section presence but not evidence authenticity

security_findings.action: Enforce `realpath`-based repo-root allowlisting, reject symlinks and `..` escapes, and add regression tests for traversal/symlink scenarios.
security_findings.risk: The spec requires avoiding out-of-scope files but does not define canonicalization/symlink handling, leaving room for traversal or unintended file access during gate evaluation.
security_findings.title: Out-of-scope file guard lacks explicit canonical path/symlink controls

product_findings.action: Enforce canonical repo-root path checks and symlink boundary rejection, and make autofix transactional with rollback before any restage; on failure, explicitly confirm that no out-of-scope or partial changes remain staged.
product_findings.risk: If drift inputs escape approved paths or partially apply before failure, users can unknowingly commit unrelated changes and lose trust in autofix behavior.
product_findings.title: Scoped autofix can still violate user expectations without explicit fail-safe boundaries

product_findings.action: Add explicit negative fixtures for `../` traversal, absolute-path injection, symlink escape, and delimiter edge cases; assert non-zero exit, explicit remediation text, and zero out-of-scope index/worktree changes.
product_findings.risk: Broad test-suite execution can pass without validating traversal, absolute-path, or symlink bypass attempts, allowing regressions that impact user repos.
product_findings.title: Current test contract does not prove guardrails against adversarial drift inputs

product_findings.action: Add parity tests that run identical drift fixtures through precommit and CI/autofix paths and assert identical classification, exit codes, and user-facing remediation output.
product_findings.risk: Users may pass locally but fail in CI (or vice versa) with different classifications or remediation guidance, creating workflow confusion and rework.
product_findings.title: Local precommit and CI autofix parity is not explicitly acceptance-tested

product_findings.action: PO/end-user must approve manual-only categories (minimum: bi-directional conflicts, concurrent template+living edits, semantic multi-file conflicts) and required remediation steps before completion.
product_findings.risk: Without an approved manual-only denylist, ambiguous or two-sided drift may be auto-fixed unexpectedly, conflicting with intended UX and risk posture.
product_findings.title: Manual-review drift categories are not finalized for human sign-off

product_findings.action: Standardize blocked/recovered CLI messaging to include exact files, reason classification, safe rerun command, and stage status; lock this with automated output-contract tests.
product_findings.risk: Fail-closed outcomes without standardized file-level diagnostics and next commands increase repeat failure loops and reduce workflow clarity.
product_findings.title: Blocked-state UX lacks a deterministic recovery guidance contract

product_findings.action: Define baseline and target thresholds for drift-related failures/manual interventions and review in human validation after initial rollout.
product_findings.risk: The team may ship without proving reduction in drift-related manual intervention and failed runs.
product_findings.title: Post-release user value measurement is underspecified

security_findings.action: Implement fail-closed path controls in the autofix path selection/restage flow: resolve real paths, enforce repo-root + approved-scope prefix checks, reject boundary-crossing symlinks, and emit explicit remediation.
security_findings.risk: The feature requires scoped repairs and blocking out-of-scope changes, but the provided spec/tasks do not require canonical-path and symlink-boundary enforcement. Drift inputs like ../, absolute paths, or symlink escapes could modify/restage files outside intended scope.
security_findings.title: Scoped autofix boundary is not explicitly hardened against path escape

security_findings.action: Add explicit automated tests for ../ traversal, absolute-path injection, symlink escape, and path-delimiter edge cases; assert non-zero exit, explicit diagnostics, and zero out-of-scope index/worktree changes.
security_findings.risk: Acceptance includes blocking out-of-scope modification attempts, but execution evidence only names broad test targets and does not document adversarial fixtures. A scope-bypass regression could pass without proving this control.
security_findings.title: Security-negative drift tests are not explicitly required by current test contract

security_findings.action: Make autofix transactional: classify all drift first, stage only after full validation, and rollback touched scoped files/index on any error or ambiguity before returning failure.
security_findings.risk: Docs require fail-closed on ambiguous/unresolved drift, but do not define rollback if partial edits/staging occurred before failure. Partial staged state can leak unintended changes into later commits.
security_findings.title: Fail-closed behavior lacks explicit transactional rollback semantics

security_findings.action: Define and approve a manual-only denylist in feature docs, then enforce it in code/tests (minimum: bi-directional conflicts, template+living concurrent edits, multi-file semantic conflicts) with hard block and human remediation steps.
security_findings.risk: The open question on which drift categories must stay manual leaves policy ambiguity. Without explicit categories, high-risk two-sided/semantic drift may be auto-fixed heuristically.
security_findings.title: Manual-only drift categories remain undefined

product_findings.action: PO must choose and document the default trigger matrix (before each `make feature`, PR CI behavior, and override rules) and approve it in feature docs.
product_findings.risk: Without a default policy for when to run the smoke test, users can skip it before real work and lose the core regression-prevention value.
product_findings.title: Smoke-test trigger policy is unresolved

product_findings.action: Implement a required summary schema with `stage`, `failed_invariant`, `evidence_pointer_or_log_path`, and `next_action`; add automated tests that assert schema presence for baseline-fail and gate-violation scenarios.
product_findings.risk: Pass/fail output can be technically correct but still non-actionable, causing slow troubleshooting and repeated failed runs.
product_findings.title: Failure summary contract is not strict enough for fast recovery

product_findings.action: Add explicit release-gate text in feature docs requiring closure evidence for SEC-20-001 through SEC-20-004 before marking this feature complete.
product_findings.risk: If SEC-20-001 to SEC-20-004 are not part of completion criteria, users may receive a false-safe smoke result that can leak data or be bypassed.
product_findings.title: Product DoD does not explicitly gate on security blocker closure

product_findings.action: Define concrete runtime budgets for local and CI runs and enforce/report them in automated tests.
product_findings.risk: A qualitative 'bounded runtime' can drift upward and make frequent use impractical, reducing adoption.
product_findings.title: Runtime bound lacks measurable threshold

product_findings.action: Run a human-validation checklist on one resumed and one fresh run to confirm status wording is unambiguous and evidence pointers are easy to follow.
product_findings.risk: Users may misinterpret resumed vs newly executed stages, leading to incorrect trust in outcomes.
product_findings.title: Human readability of resume/skip/repair states is not explicitly validated

security_findings.action: In `tools/pc-feature`, enforce a strict ID format, canonicalize resolved paths, and fail closed if any path is outside approved roots. Add tests for `../`, absolute paths, and symlink-hop attempts.
security_findings.risk: The feature depends on artifacts under `logs/<WI>/` and offload pointers, but the provided docs do not require strict validation of `<WI>`/scenario IDs. Traversal values could read/write outside intended directories.
security_findings.title: Unsanitized work-item identifiers can escape log/offload directories

security_findings.action: Execute tests without shell, compare normalized argv against a structured allowlist, and reject metacharacters/multi-command forms. Add negative tests for `;`, `&&`, `|`, and `$()` bypass attempts.
security_findings.risk: Docs require Allowed Tests enforcement but only describe command whitelisting; they do not require shell-free execution or canonical argv matching. Chaining/metacharacter payloads can execute non-allowed commands.
security_findings.title: Allowed Tests policy can be bypassed without shell-safe command validation

security_findings.action: Implement log/summarization redaction for common secret patterns and sensitive keys, then add fixture tests with seeded fake secrets to verify masking in both logs and pass/fail output.
security_findings.risk: The workflow explicitly offloads noisy output and emits evidence pointers, but no redaction requirement is defined. Credentials or sensitive env-derived values can leak into `.offload` files and summaries.
security_findings.title: No secret-redaction control for evidence pointers and structured logs

security_findings.action: Add automated tests that alter resume/state/evidence artifacts and assert fail-closed behavior (no stage skip, no completion) until integrity checks pass.
security_findings.risk: Acceptance scenarios include resume behavior, but the provided test scope does not require adversarial cases (tampered resume state or forged stage evidence). This can permit false PASS via manipulated artifacts.
security_findings.title: Resume-path security is untested against tampered state/artifacts

product_findings.action: Define a required proposal schema for user review: problem evidence, suggested change, expected user impact, affected scope, confidence, and rollback note; reject incomplete proposals.
product_findings.risk: Current spec does not define the minimum proposal content needed for confident approval, so users can receive vague proposals that are hard to evaluate and easy to reject incorrectly.
product_findings.title: Proposal contract is not actionable for end users

product_findings.action: Specify and implement deterministic state transitions and CLI messages for approve/reject/defer/resubmit, explicitly aligned with fail-closed approval for the current proposal identity/integrity.
product_findings.risk: The feature mentions a human gate but does not fully define approve/reject/defer/resubmit behavior, creating ambiguous outcomes and inconsistent reruns.
product_findings.title: Human-gate decision flow is incomplete

product_findings.action: Add blocking automated tests for reject persistence, rerun idempotency/deduplication, approved-and-applied no-op behavior, and stale proposal handling, alongside required security abuse-case tests.
product_findings.risk: With only happy-path plus one edge case, regressions can re-surface rejected proposals, duplicate proposals on rerun, or mishandle already-applied approvals.
product_findings.title: Required tests miss user-critical workflow branches

product_findings.action: Add measurable acceptance criteria: deterministic ordering, proposal count limits, explicit rationale per proposal, and auditable link from failure evidence to proposal to human decision.
product_findings.risk: The feature can be marked done through documentation completion without proving decision quality, predictability, or traceability for end users.
product_findings.title: Acceptance criteria are not measurable for user value

product_findings.action: Require PO/end-user validation using realistic cases to confirm approval prompts clearly show proposal identity, impacted scope, and explicit y/n intent with no default-accept behavior.
product_findings.risk: Users may approve incorrect proposals if impact scope and proposal identity are not clearly understood under real failure scenarios.
product_findings.title: Approval UX clarity needs explicit human validation

product_findings.action: Define deterministic prioritization and suppression rules (including max proposals per run and repeated-failure dedupe) to keep output reviewable.
product_findings.risk: Too many low-signal proposals can reduce trust and lead to blanket rejection, weakening the learning loop.
product_findings.title: Proposal noise-control policy is undefined

security_findings.action: Implement an explicit proposal state machine (`proposed|approved|rejected|applied`) and block any apply operation unless approval exists for the current proposal ID/hash.
security_findings.risk: The feature summary says proposals have a human gate, but the spec/tasks do not require a deny-by-default approval state. A patch could accidentally allow apply paths without explicit approval.
security_findings.title: Human gate is not specified as fail-closed

security_findings.action: Enforce a strict schema for proposal payloads, allowlist operation types, reject unknown fields, and treat proposal text strictly as data (never executable input).
security_findings.risk: Workflow E transforms failures into proposals, but no schema/allowlist is defined. Malicious payloads could be interpreted as executable instructions or unsafe file operations.
security_findings.title: Proposal content validation is undefined

security_findings.action: Add secret-redaction before proposal generation/storage/display, covering common key/token patterns and sensitive local path fragments.
security_findings.risk: Workflow C offloads noisy command output and Learning Loop consumes failure context. Without redaction controls, tokens/credentials/path secrets can be persisted in proposal artifacts.
security_findings.title: Secrets can leak from offloaded logs into proposals

security_findings.action: Persist proposal hash with approval metadata and verify hash equality at apply time; fail closed on mismatch and log a security event.
security_findings.risk: Docs require logs but do not require tamper detection between approved content and applied content. Approved proposals could be modified after approval.
security_findings.title: Approval record is not bound to proposal integrity

security_findings.action: Add blocking automated tests for: unapproved proposal denied, tampered proposal denied, malicious payload rejected, and secret-redaction enforcement.
security_findings.risk: Task-003 only mandates happy path + one edge case, so critical security regressions can pass feature completion unnoticed.
security_findings.title: Security abuse-case tests are missing from required test scope

security_findings.action: Perform human validation that approval UI shows proposal ID/hash, impacted scope, explicit `y/n`, and no default-accept behavior.
security_findings.risk: Human gate exists, but docs do not require verification that approval prompts clearly show proposal identity/scope, increasing accidental approval risk.
security_findings.title: Human approval UX safety needs explicit validation

features.feature_title: End-to-end workflow smoke test with a synthetic feature

product_findings.action: Define and implement a strict output contract for success/failure that includes stage status, resume state (resumed/skipped/repaired/new), and required evidence pointers.
product_findings.risk: The feature does not define the exact CLI signals a PO should use to confirm end-to-end success, so runs can look successful while gates/evidence are incomplete.
product_findings.title: Missing deterministic user-facing pass criteria

product_findings.action: Add automated tests for first run vs rerun vs interrupted-resume that assert deterministic outcomes, no duplicate stage effects, and stable evidence references.
product_findings.risk: Without explicit repeated-run assertions, users may see duplicate, drifting, or inconsistent outcomes and lose trust in workflow safety.
product_findings.title: Idempotent rerun and resume behavior is not acceptance-tested

product_findings.action: Define a mandatory scenario matrix and automate it: happy path plus at least one negative/loop case for each critical gate and handoff.
product_findings.risk: A single happy-path smoke can pass while key real-world branches (approval block, rejection loop, recovery flow) remain broken for end users.
product_findings.title: Smoke coverage omits critical user workflow branches

product_findings.action: Add an explicit clarification gate with fail-closed status, owner routing, and required log evidence before execution can continue.
product_findings.risk: The spec says to seek PO clarification on ambiguity but does not define blocked state, ownership, or logging, which can cause scope drift and rework.
product_findings.title: PO clarification path is underspecified

product_findings.action: Run and record a human-validation checklist covering gate prompts, blocked labels, remediation text, and final run summary readability before approval.
product_findings.risk: Even if automation passes, PO users may still misinterpret prompts, blocked states, and remediation actions during real operation.
product_findings.title: No required human sign-off for workflow clarity

security_findings.action: Add a centralized sanitizer before any log/offload write (mask common secret patterns and sensitive env keys), and add regression tests that inject synthetic secrets and verify masked output in both destinations.
security_findings.risk: Workflow C requires writing noisy output to `.offload/<id>.txt` and `logs/<WI>/<step>.log`, but the feature docs define no masking/redaction rule; credentials or tokens printed by tests/CLI can be stored and later committed.
security_findings.title: No secret-redaction control for offloaded and structured logs

security_findings.action: Enforce strict allowlist validation for path segments, canonicalize and verify base-directory containment, reject invalid/absolute/traversal inputs, and add tests for `../`, absolute paths, and symlink escape attempts.
security_findings.risk: The documented paths use runtime placeholders (`<WI>`, `<step>`, `<id>`) without explicit input constraints; unsanitized values can escape target directories or overwrite unintended files.
security_findings.title: Path traversal risk in log/offload file generation

security_findings.action: Add automated smoke tests that prove fail-closed behavior: blocked status (`Awaiting PO Approval` where applicable), non-zero exit, and no patch/test/commit stage execution until required approvals/evidence exist.
security_findings.risk: Workflows require blocking at HIGH-risk approval, Plan Reviewer approval, and commit evidence gates, but tasks do not require explicit automated assertions that downstream stages cannot execute when gates are unmet.
security_findings.title: Fail-closed gate behavior is specified but not security-tested

security_findings.action: Harden resume metadata with integrity validation (state/evidence binding), fail closed on mismatch, and force re-run of guarded stages when validation fails.
security_findings.risk: Workflow D allows skipping completed stages on resume; without integrity checks tying state to real evidence, a modified state file can falsely mark review/test/report gates as complete.
security_findings.title: Resume-state tampering can bypass required checks

security_findings.action: Constrain synthetic execution to an isolated temp worktree and enforce an allowlisted command/file-write scope; add validation that reruns only touch expected artifacts.
security_findings.risk: The feature targets end-to-end execution but docs do not require isolation boundaries for synthetic runs, creating risk of unintended writes outside expected test artifacts.
security_findings.title: Synthetic smoke run lacks explicit isolation guardrails
